summary: pi already has strong, code-verified support for the strape goals. CLAUDE.md is a first-class fallback context file (not a hack) with a hardcoded, non-configurable precedence; Claude Code skills work unmodified via a documented settings.json entry (no code change needed); OpenAI and xAI/Grok are both first-class providers (Responses API for OpenAI, Chat-Completions API for most Grok models + Responses API for grok-4.5) with symmetric default-model treatment to Anthropic; and pi ships an explicit, intentional white-label/fork mechanism (package.json piConfig.name/configDir + pi.unregisterProvider()) that lets strape rebrand and trim providers via config/extension instead of forking core files, which directly serves the "easy to pull upstream updates" requirement.
key_facts: Context-file precedence is hardcoded per-directory in loadContextFileFromDir(): candidates = ["AGENTS.override.md","AGENTS.md","AGENTS.MD","CLAUDE.md","CLAUDE.MD"], first existing match wins and the function returns immediately (packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:70-89). If a directory has BOTH AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md always wins in that directory; CLAUDE.md is only used when no AGENTS*.md variant exists there.

This precedence is NOT configurable via settings.json, env var, or CLI flag - the only lever is the all-or-nothing --no-context-files/-nc CLI flag (SDK option noContextFiles), documented at packages/coding-agent/src/cli/args.ts:287 and wired at resource-loader.ts:172,515-521. Changing the per-directory resolution order itself would require editing the candidates array in source.

loadProjectContextFiles() (resource-loader.ts:118-156) walks from cwd up to filesystem root via a dirname() loop (lines 139-151, terminates when parentDir===currentDir), loading one context file per directory (ancestors first, cwd's own file last), PLUS a separate 'global' context file from agentDir (default ~/.pi/agent) checked once via the same candidate list (lines 128-132). A global CLAUDE.md would need to live at ~/.pi/agent/CLAUDE.md, not Claude Code's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md - global reuse needs a symlink/copy, but project-level CLAUDE.md files are picked up automatically with zero configuration.
A worktree-shadowing rule (findShadowedContextFile, resource-loader.ts:100-116) prevents double-loading a linked git worktree's own context file when it duplicates the main repo's.

CONFIG_DIR_NAME = pkg.piConfig?.configDir || ".pi" (packages/coding-agent/src/config.ts:491), read from packages/coding-agent/package.json's piConfig:{configDir:".pi"} field (package.json:6-8) at import time - a build-time constant, not overridable by env var or settings.json at runtime.

APP_NAME = pkg.piConfig?.name || "pi" (config.ts:489); ENV_AGENT_DIR is derived from APP_NAME as `${APP_NAME.toUpperCase()}_CODING_AGENT_DIR` (config.ts:495), e.g. PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR by default - renaming via piConfig.name would automatically rename this env var, and the default ~/.pi/agent path (config.ts:520) becomes ~/.<name>/agent.

pi already has a deliberate, intentional white-label/fork mechanism: packages/coding-agent/src/cli/startup-ui.ts:26-42 defines OFFICIAL_PACKAGE_NAME/OFFICIAL_APP_NAME/OFFICIAL_CONFIG_DIR_NAME and isOfficialDistribution(), used at startup-ui.ts:115-121 to skip the official first-time-setup/telemetry flow for any distribution that changes package name, app name, or config dir - i.e. renaming pi->strape via package.json's piConfig is an anticipated, supported path.

Skills discovery (packages/coding-agent/src/core/skills.ts + packages/coding-agent/src/core/package-manager.ts) only auto-scans: <agentDir>/skills (default ~/.pi/agent/skills), <cwd>/<CONFIG_DIR_NAME>/skills (default .pi/skills) - skills.ts:430-433; PLUS a harness-neutral convention .agents/skills walked from cwd up to the git repo root (or filesystem root) and ~/.agents/skills globally - package-manager.ts:435-454 (collectAncestorAgentsSkillDirs) and package-manager.ts:2375-2478 (addAutoDiscoveredResources). .claude/skills is NOT in this auto-scanned list.

docs/skills.md:43-62 explicitly documents the supported way to reuse Claude Code / Codex skills: add their directories to the skills array in settings.json, e.g. global ~/.pi/agent/settings.json: {"skills": ["~/.claude/skills", "~/.codex/skills"]}, or project .pi/settings.json: {"skills": ["../.claude/skills"]}. This is a pure config change - no code fork needed to satisfy goal #4 for skills.

Skill file format is compatible: frontmatter fields are name (lowercase a-z0-9-hyphen, <=64 chars, but unlike the Agent Skills spec pi does NOT require name==parent-dir-name - skills.ts:296-301, docs/skills.md:143,157) and description (required, <=1024 chars, skills.ts:117-127). Discovery: a directory containing SKILL.md is a skill root and is not recursed further (skills.ts:160-171,194-221) - identical to Claude Code's SKILL.md convention. Standard Claude Code SKILL.md files (name+description frontmatter) work unmodified.

Gap vs Claude Code skills: allowed-tools frontmatter field is documented as 'experimental' (docs/skills.md:148) but is NOT actually parsed or enforced anywhere in code - grep -rn "allowed-tools" packages/coding-agent/src returns zero hits; the field is silently ignored (falls under 'unknown frontmatter fields are ignored', docs/skills.md:184). pi additionally auto-registers every skill as a /skill:name slash command with argument-appending ('User: <args>', docs/skills.md:82) - a pi-specific extra, not a gap. Neither system has skill-level hooks.

OpenAI provider (packages/ai/src/providers/openai.ts:6-15): id "openai", baseUrl https://api.openai.com/v1, auth via OPENAI_API_KEY env var (envApiKeyAuth, line 11), API = openai-responses only (Responses API, not legacy Chat Completions).

xAI provider (packages/ai/src/providers/xai.ts:8-28): id "xai", baseUrl https://api.x.ai/v1, auth via XAI_API_KEY env var (line 14) OR OAuth subscription login 'Sign in with SuperGrok or X Premium' (lines 15-20, isSubscription:true) - documented in docs/providers.md:42-45 (/login xai). Registers BOTH openai-completions and openai-responses APIs (lines 23-26).

Per-model API assignment for xAI is in packages/ai/scripts/generate-models.ts:1608-1635: only grok-4.5 (XAI_RESPONSES_MODEL_ID, line 407) uses the Responses API (with custom effort-level map XAI_RESPONSES_EFFORT_LEVEL_MAP and supportsLongCacheRetention:false, lines 415-421); every other tool-calling Grok model (models with m.tool_call !== true are filtered out entirely, line 1612) uses openai-completions. Older/non-reasoning variants (grok-3, grok-3-fast, grok-4.20-*-non-reasoning, grok-code-fast-1) are excluded from the built-in catalog (XAI_BUILTIN_EXCLUDED_MODEL_IDS, generate-models.ts:408-414).

Reasoning/tool-calling/streaming quality for the OpenAI Responses path (packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses.ts) is mature: reasoning effort levels (minimal/low/medium/high/xhigh/max) mapped per-model via thinkingLevelMap (lines 312-327), xAI-specific handling for reasoning.encrypted_content inclusion (line 327: if (model.provider === "xai") params.include = ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]), streaming via AssistantMessageEventStream (lines 106,158-193), constrained/grammar tool calling support (openai-completions.ts / constrained-sampling.ts).

The models.dev-sourced catalog data (packages/ai/src/providers/data/*.json) is git-ignored (.gitignore:11 packages/ai/src/providers/data/) and regenerated at build time by npm run generate-models (packages/ai/package.json:52-57), which fetches from https://models.dev/api.json (generate-models.ts:1289) plus several provider APIs (OpenRouter, NVIDIA, Vercel AI Gateway, etc., lines 973-1057) - a build-time supply-chain touchpoint (not a CLI runtime dependency), relevant to strape's security-review goal.

defaultModelPerProvider table (packages/coding-agent/src/core/model-resolver.ts:20-40) treats openai (gpt-5.5) and xai (grok-4.5) as first-class defaults on equal footing with anthropic (claude-opus-4-8) - confirms symmetric product-level support, not an afterthought.

Provider list is fully pluggable at runtime without touching packages/ai: pi.registerProvider()/pi.unregisterProvider(name) extension API (docs/custom-provider.md:3,188-190) lets an extension remove Anthropic (and any other unwanted provider) or add fully custom providers/OAuth flows, and builtinProviders() (packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts:89-132) is a simple flat array trivially filterable if a fork is preferred instead.

Anthropic-specific code touches only about 10 files in packages/coding-agent/src, mostly narrow quirks: cache-control format literal in model-config.ts:99,123 (cacheControlFormat: "anthropic"), Bedrock/Anthropic default model IDs in model-resolver.ts:21,23, an opt-out warning warnings.anthropicExtraUsage (settings.md:97-109) for subscription extra-usage billing, and Anthropic-specific image-resize limits (utils/image-resize-core.ts). None of this blocks removing/hiding the Anthropic provider for strape.

settings.json exposes defaultProvider/defaultModel/defaultThinkingLevel (docs/settings.md:26-36) and a skills string[] array supporting globs, ~, and force-include/exclude (docs/settings.md:239-248) - this settings surface alone is sufficient to deliver goal #4 for skills (add ~/.claude/skills / project ../.claude/skills) without any code changes; there is no equivalent settings knob for context-file naming/precedence (goal #4 for CLAUDE.md already works out of the box via the built-in candidate list, no setting needed).
risks: Global CLAUDE.md reuse is incomplete: pi's global fallback only checks <agentDir>/CLAUDE.md (default ~/.pi/agent/CLAUDE.md, resource-loader.ts:128), not Claude Code's ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. Users relying on a global (all-projects) CLAUDE.md in Claude Code will need a symlink/copy step for strape; only project-level CLAUDE.md files 'just work' via the ancestor walk.

CONFIG_DIR_NAME (".pi"/project folder name) is a compile-time constant sourced from packages/coding-agent/package.json's piConfig.configDir, not an env var or settings.json field - renaming pi's on-disk project folder (.pi -> .strape) requires editing/forking that package.json field (and rebuilding), which is a merge-conflict-prone touchpoint on every upstream pull unless isolated as a patch or maintained fork branch.

allowed-tools skill frontmatter is documented as 'experimental' but unimplemented (no enforcement in code) - any strape security model that assumes skills are tool-restricted via that field would be a false sense of security; skills can invoke arbitrary tools regardless of allowed-tools.

Model catalog data (grok/openai pricing, context windows, capability flags) is fetched at build time from https://models.dev/api.json and other third-party APIs and is not checked into git - a supply-chain surface for strape's security review (integrity/pinning of that fetch, staleness/availability of models.dev) even though it doesn't run at CLI runtime for end users.

The 40+ provider files in packages/ai/src/providers/ (many for niche China-market/token-plan providers) increase the codebase's dependency/audit surface if strape imports packages/ai wholesale; trimming via builtinProviders() filtering or pi.unregisterProvider() reduces runtime attack surface but does not reduce what ships in node_modules/the bundle unless the unused provider files are also excluded from the build.
recommendations: For goal #4 (reuse CLAUDE.md/.claude/skills) do NOT fork resource-loader.ts or skills.ts: CLAUDE.md already works per-directory/per-project with zero config, and skills can be pointed at ~/.claude/skills / ../.claude/skills purely via settings.json's skills array (docs/skills.md:43-62) - this is the lowest-effort, most-maintainable path and requires no upstream divergence.

If a true global CLAUDE.md (not per-project) is desired, either symlink ~/.pi/agent/CLAUDE.md -> ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, or point the agent dir at a location that already contains it, rather than patching the candidates array in resource-loader.ts:71.

For goal #1 (Grok + OpenAI only, no Anthropic) prefer a small first-party extension calling pi.unregisterProvider("anthropic") (and other unwanted providers) over deleting files from packages/ai/src/providers - this keeps 100% of packages/ai upstreamable/mergeable (goal #5) and is reversible/toggleable.

For goal #3 (rename pi->strape) use the already-designed white-label hooks: set piConfig.name/piConfig.configDir in a forked coding-agent package.json (or via a build-time patch step) rather than renaming identifiers throughout src - this is exactly the seam upstream built (startup-ui.ts's isOfficialDistribution check) and keeps future git pull/rebase friction minimal.

Track packages/coding-agent/package.json's piConfig block and packages/ai/src/providers/all.ts's builtinProviders() array as the two intentional 'customization points' to diff/reapply on each upstream sync, since both are small, stable, deliberately-designed extension seams rather than deep patches.

During the dependency/supply-chain security review, explicitly scope whether packages/ai/src/providers/data/ generation (models.dev fetch, OpenRouter/NVIDIA/Vercel fetches in generate-models.ts) is part of strape's build pipeline; if so, pin/verify that fetch or vendor a reviewed snapshot instead of fetching live at every build.

Explicitly decide whether allowed-tools needs to matter for strape's threat model; if skill-level tool restriction is required, that needs new code in skills.ts/agent-session.ts since upstream does not enforce it today - treat as a design gap rather than assuming parity with any harness that does enforce it.
